_what: Every India figure the Teach section is allowed to use. A writer may use ANY entry here and NOTHING else. It exists because the compendium arrived teaching Britain, and the fix for that is not a better-sounding sentence — it is a figure somebody can check. Each entry names its publisher, its publication and the year it describes.
_rule: If a claim you want to make is not in this file, you may not make it. Write around it, or ask for the figure to be sourced and added. Do not estimate, do not round, do not carry a number over from another country, and do not write 'studies show'.

figures.plain: Forest cover is 21.76% of India's land area; with tree cover outside forests it reaches 25.17%.
figures.publisher: Forest Survey of India, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
figures.publication: India State of Forest Report 2023, Volume 1, Table 2.3

figures.plain: Between 2021 and 2023 forest cover rose by 156.41 km2 and tree cover by 1,289.4 km2 — a small net gain, and most of it is tree cover outside forests rather than forest.
figures.publication: India State of Forest Report 2023, Table 2.2

figures.plain: Lightning killed 2,825 people in India in 2024 — more than any other force of nature, and it is on no school syllabus.
figures.publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
figures.publication: Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 2024, Table 1.0
figures.caution: These are RECORDED deaths — a reporting authority attributed them to a cause and filed them. Not a model, and not the same as the number a hazard actually killed.

figures.plain: Recorded heat and sun-stroke deaths more than doubled in a year — 804 in 2023, 1,832 in 2024.
7,903 deaths in India in 2024 were recorded against forces of nature, up 22.6% on 2023.
figures.publication: Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 2024, Table 1.0

figures.plain: India generates 1,70,339 tonnes of solid waste a day and collects 1,56,449 of it — a 92% collection rate.
figures.publication: Annual Report on Solid Waste Management 2021-2022, section 2.1

figures.plain: 54% of India's waste is treated or processed and 24% goes to landfill. The remaining 22% — 37,373 tonnes every day — is unaccounted for.
figures.publication: Annual Report on Solid Waste Management 2021-2022, section 2.1
figures.caution: The 22% is the report's own residual, not a separate measurement. It is the strongest single fact in this theme: a fifth of the country's waste has no recorded destination.

figures.plain: India takes out 247.18 billion cubic metres of groundwater a year against 407.88 it can safely take — a stage of extraction of 60.6%. Around a quarter of the country's 6,762 assessment units are Over-exploited, Critical or Semi-Critical.
figures.unit: billion cubic metres per year, and %
figures.publisher: Central Ground Water Board, Ministry of Jal Shakti
figures.publication: National Compilation on Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India, 2025 (published November 2025)
figures.caution: A block is a large area — a Safe block can contain a failing neighbourhood. And a stage below 100% does not mean the water is fit to drink; that is a quality question this table does not answer.

figures.plain: Punjab takes out 156 litres for every 100 its aquifers put back. Rajasthan takes 147. Delhi takes 92.
figures.publication: National Compilation on Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India, 2025
figures.caution: Above 100% means stored water is being spent — the aquifer is being drawn down, not just used.

figures.plain: The Yamuna leaves Yamunotri with 11.2 mg/L of dissolved oxygen. At four stations in a row in Delhi it reads 0.3 mg/L, which is the lowest figure the method can report — so the true value is at or below it. The standard for bathing water is above 5.0 mg/L.
figures.publication: National Water Quality Monitoring Programme, river Yamuna water quality data 2025
figures.caution: Never write 0.0. The figure is the reporting floor — say 'at or below 0.3'. This is a rule on this site, not a style preference.

themes_not_yet_sourced.note: No figure for these has been read from a primary Indian source yet. CEA publishes installed capacity only as an Excel workbook, and nothing for food or the SDGs has been obtained. A writer working on these themes uses Indian EXAMPLES and Indian context, and states no numbers at all.

already_in_the_air_theme: The air theme was rewritten separately and already carries CPCB's six AQI bands, the NAAQS 2009 limits and the IIT Kanpur / TERI-ARAI source-apportionment ranges. Do not restate or alter those — see data/teach/themes/blowing-in-the-wind.json.

verified_context._what: Non-numeric India claims added by the copy pass, each checked against a source before publication. These are CONTEXT, not figures — a writer may state them. Anything not on this list and not in `figures` may not be stated.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: Prof. Rajagopalan Vasudevan of Thiagarajar College of Engineering, Madurai, developed the shredded-plastic-with-bitumen road. First laid on his campus in 2002, patented 2006, Padma Shri 2018.
Used beverage cartons are recycled in India into PolyAl corrugated roofing sheets.
checked_2026_09_12.note: Eastern Cargo (Gujarat) since 2016; Sabar Dairy cow-shed roofs; Saahas Zero Waste processes cartons at scale.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: Olive ridley hatchlings were seen at Versova beach, Mumbai, in March 2018 after about twenty years, following Afroz Shah's cleanup begun October 2015.
checked_2026_09_12.note: ★ DO NOT assert the cleanup CAUSED the nesting — that framing has been fact-checked as misleading. Say the hatchlings were seen again. Also ignore the '9 million tonnes' figure that circulates with this story; it is absurd for a 2.5km beach.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: Seelampur (Delhi) is India's largest informal e-waste dismantling market; Moradabad processes material sent on from it.
checked_2026_09_12.note: ★ Smelting and the most polluting processing have largely MOVED OUT of Seelampur to Loni and Moradabad. Dismantling and acid work happen in Seelampur. Do not put every process in one place. NCPCR has published a fact-finding report on children working in both.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: The Ghazipur landfill in Delhi collapsed on 1 September 2017, killing two people, when the mound was about 50 metres high against a 20-metre limit.
checked_2026_09_12.note: Press-reported (Tribune, Gulf News, Hindustan Times), not an official statistic — attribute it as reported if the figures are used. The theme currently states this qualitatively, which is also fine.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: The foam on Bellandur lake, Bengaluru, caught fire in May 2015.
The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 require household segregation.
checked_2026_09_12.note: Cited as Rule 15(b) inside CPCB's own Annual Report on Solid Waste Management 2021-22 — the same document the waste figures come from.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: India banned identified single-use plastic items from 1 July 2022.
checked_2026_09_12.note: Press Information Bureau; made under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021, notified 12 August 2021. Items include cutlery, straws, thermocol decoration and plastic stirrers.

checked_2026_09_12.claim: Producers carry take-back responsibility for e-waste (EPR).
checked_2026_09_12.note: The writer deliberately gave no year. Leave it that way unless someone checks the E-Waste (Management) Rules.
